title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in l
summary: Deep-learning models quantified immune cells and lymphoid structures in lung squamous-cell carcinoma samples. In a 40-patient discovery cohort, neoadjuvant-treated cases had fewer stromal plasma cells and fewer mature tertiary or secondary lymphoid structures in specified compartments; an independent 458-patient cohort linked stromal plasma-cell density and lymphocyte–plasma-cell colocalization with longer survival. The observational comparison does not show that treatment caused these differences.
ai_technology: Deep-learning tissue and cell models quantified immune-cell densities, co-localization, and TLS/SLS maturity from H&E slides, supporting comparison of tumor and lymph-node immune architecture.
organization: University of Pennsylvania; University of California, San Francisco

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: The TLS model was evaluated on held-out annotated slides; the study also tested survival associations in an independent 458-patient cohort.
evidence.unknown: Small observational treatment comparison; model errors and cohort differences limit interpretation, and causal treatment effects are not established.
